SearchWatermark: Search files and folders... (leave empty to browse everything)
StatusChooseOption: Choose an option to start scanning
ContentSearchWatermark: Text to search inside files — press Enter...
SelectFolderOrScanAll: Select a folder or scan the whole PC
ContentReadyPrompt: Ready — type text and press Enter to search
SelectFolderFirstContent: Select a folder to search first
JobFinishedWithErrors: Finished, but some items were skipped
JobErrorIntoItself: a folder can't be copied into itself
JobClipboardEmpty: The clipboard has no copied files
ConflictApplyToAll: Do this for all remaining conflicts
NameSearchSubtitle: Find files and folders by name — results appear as you type.
ContentSearchSubtitle: Search for text inside documents, code and spreadsheets.
SettingsSubtitle: Choose how Grepdesk integrates with your system.
ExplorerMenuDescription: Add Grepdesk entries to Explorer's right-click menu. Stored for the current user only, no admin rights needed. On Windows 11 they appear under "Show more options".
FileManagerMenuDescription: Add Grepdesk entries to your file manager's right-click menu.
IntegrationUnsupported: Right-click menu integration isn't available on this platform yet.
FeatureOpenWithHint: On folders: open Grepdesk with that folder ready to search.
FeatureExtractHint: On .zip files: "Extract here" and "Extract to folder".
FeatureCompressHint: On files and folders: create a zip archive.
FeaturePasteHint: On folders: fast copy or move of files you copied/cut in Explorer.
ResultsShowingTop: {0:N0} results for "{1}" — showing the first {2:N0} in this order
LanguageDescription: Language of the app and of its Explorer menu entries.
ShowPreviewHint: Shows the selected result next to the list: images, the start of text and code files, and the text of documents. Hidden automatically when the window is narrow.
PreviewEmpty: Select a result to preview it here
PreviewFailed: This file could not be read
PreviewUnavailable: No preview for this file type
AllItemsShowingTop: {0:N0} items in the scanned folders — showing the first {1:N0} in this order
ShortcutMoveToResults: Move between the search box and the results
ShortcutShowInFolder: Show the selected result in its folder
ShortcutTrash: Move the selected result to the Recycle Bin
ShortcutEscape: Back to the search box (clears it when already there)
TrashConfirmFolder: Move the folder "{0}" and everything in it to the Recycle Bin?
TrashFailed: Could not move to the Recycle Bin
PreviewPdfNoText: This PDF has no text layer (probably a scanned document)
FileCopied: "{0}" copied — paste it anywhere in Explorer
ShortcutCopyFile: Copy the selected file itself (paste in Explorer)
DiskSubtitle: What is filling your drive: by kind of file, by folder, and the largest files.
DiskEmpty: Pick a drive and click Analyze. The first analysis scans the whole drive, which can take a minute or two on a large disk. If you already scanned the entire PC on the file name page, that scan is reused.
DiskAnalyzed: Analyzed at {0}. Sizes reflect that moment; analyze again after big changes.
DiskNoteUnreadable: {0} could not be read: other users' folders, System Volume Information, restore points and file system data.
DiskNoteCloud: {0} of online-only cloud files (OneDrive etc.) is not counted: those don't use this disk.
DiskCategoriesHint: Click a kind to list its largest files. Where a file lives decides its kind first: a video inside a game folder counts as the game.
DiskGroupsTitleSystem: What takes space in the system
DiskGroupsSubtitle: {0:N0} items, {1:N0} files in total. Double-click to look inside.
DiskScanChanged: The drive scan has changed since this analysis (another drive was scanned). Analyze again to browse folders.
CleanupSubtitle: Every way to get space back, in one list. Nothing is deleted until you pick it and confirm.
CleanupEmpty: Pick a drive and click Find space. If the drive was analyzed on the Disk Usage page, that scan is used and this takes a second.
CleanupReady: Pick a card to see what's in it.
CleanupTrashSummary: Deleted files still take space until the bin is emptied
CleanupDuplicatesNotSearched: Not searched yet — reads file contents
CleanupConfirmTrash: Move {0:N0} items ({1}) to the Recycle Bin?
CleanupConfirmEmptyTrash: Empty the Recycle Bin ({1})? This can't be undone.
CleanupMovedToTrash: {0} moved to the Recycle Bin — empty it to get the space back.
CleanupSkipped: {0:N0} files were in use and skipped.
CleanupNoticePermanent: Deleted permanently (not to the Recycle Bin). These are files programs recreate on their own when needed; files in use are skipped.
CleanupNoticeTrash: Moved to the Recycle Bin, so a mistake can be undone. The space comes back when the bin is emptied.
CleanupNoticeEmptyTrash: Everything in the Recycle Bin is deleted for good.
CleanupTextRecycleBin: Files you delete stay in the Recycle Bin, and keep using space, until it is emptied.
CleanupTextTempFiles: Leftovers from installers and programs in the temp folders. Anything changed in the last 24 hours isn't selected, as it may still be in use.
CleanupTextCaches: Browser, graphics driver (shader) and app caches. Programs rebuild them when needed, so the first start may be a little slower. Close your browsers to clear more of their cache.
CleanupTextDeveloperCaches: npm, pip, NuGet, Yarn and Gradle download caches, and node_modules folders. All of it can be downloaded again (npm install etc.). node_modules folders untouched for 90 days are selected; recent ones aren't.
CleanupTextDuplicates: Files with exactly the same contents (compared byte for byte), 1 MB or larger, outside game, app, system and developer folders. In each set the oldest copy is kept and the rest are selected.
CleanupTextOldDownloads: Files in Downloads older than 90 days: installers you already ran, archives you already extracted... Nothing is selected; look through and pick.
CleanupTextLargeOldFiles: Your own files over 500 MB that haven't changed in a year. Nothing is selected; look through and pick.
CleanupTextHibernation: hiberfil.sys reserves space for hibernation and Fast Startup, typically 40–75% of your RAM. If you don't use hibernation, turning it off frees all of it. Windows asks for administrator permission.
CleanupTextSystemTools: Windows Update leftovers, old driver packages and System Restore points need administrator rights and are best cleaned with Windows' own tools. Restore points are a large part of the 'unreadable' space on the Disk Usage page.
CleanupHibernateConfirm: Turn off hibernation and Fast Startup to delete hiberfil.sys? You can turn it back on with powercfg /hibernate on.
CleanupHibernateDone: Hibernation is off; hiberfil.sys has been removed.
CleanupHibernateCancelled: Administrator permission was not given; nothing changed.
CleanupNoteShaderCache: Games rebuild these on next start (brief stutter)
CleanupNoteOfflineWebData: May hold a web app's offline data
CleanupTrashing: Moving to the Recycle Bin... {2:N0}/{3:N0} items
AskButton: Ask an AI if it's safe
AskButtonTip: Makes a question about the selected items to paste into ChatGPT, Claude or another AI. Your name and personal file names are hidden.
AskTitle: Ask an AI: is it safe to delete?
AskIntro: Copy this and paste it into the AI chat you use. Nothing is sent from Grepdesk; you can edit the text first.
AskPrivacy: Privacy: your user name is replaced with <user>, profile folders with %USERPROFILE% / %LOCALAPPDATA% / %APPDATA%, and names inside Desktop, Documents, Downloads, Pictures, Videos, Music and OneDrive with <folder> / <file>.ext. Program and cache folder names are kept, since they are what the answer depends on.
AskCopied: Copied — paste it into your AI chat.
AskPromptIntro: I'm freeing up disk space on my computer ({0}). A cleanup tool suggests deleting the items below and I want to understand them before I do.
AskPromptCategory: The tool groups them as "{0}" and describes them like this: {1}
AskPromptActionDeletePermanently: The tool would delete them permanently (not to the Recycle Bin).
AskPromptActionMoveToTrash: The tool would move them to the Recycle Bin.
AskPromptActionEmptyTrash: The tool would empty the Recycle Bin.
AskPromptActionNone: The tool can't delete this itself; it would point me to a system setting.
AskPromptMore: - …and {0:N0} more items of the same kind
AskPromptQuestion: For each item: what is it, is it safe to delete, what would I lose or notice afterwards, and will it come back by itself? Tell me clearly if anything here should NOT be deleted. If you don't recognize an item or aren't sure, say "not sure" instead of guessing. Paths are anonymized: <user> is my user name, <file>/<folder> hide personal names.
